taxonomy.subtopic: MYC translocation and high-proliferation starry-sky pattern

questions.stem_html:
A 10-year-old boy develops rapidly increasing abdominal girth and early satiety over 3 weeks. Imaging shows a large ileocecal mass. Serum lactate dehydrogenase and uric acid are markedly elevated. Biopsy demonstrates a monomorphic population of medium-sized B cells with numerous interspersed tingible-body macrophages, producing a starry-sky appearance. Ki-67 staining approaches 100%.

Which genomic event most likely drives this tumor's extreme proliferative rate?

options.text_html: Juxtaposition of MYC on chromosome 8 with an immunoglobulin enhancer, most often by t(8;14)
Fusion of BCR on chromosome 22 with ABL1 on chromosome 9
Deletion of chromosome 5q with haploinsufficiency of ribosomal genes
Translocation of BCL2 to the immunoglobulin heavy-chain locus

questions.explanation_html: MYC is a transcription factor that accelerates cellular growth and metabolism. Placement beside an immunoglobulin enhancer causes constitutive MYC expression and near-total proliferative activity. The classic t(8;14) translocation moves MYC next to the immunoglobulin heavy-chain enhancer, driving the explosive growth of Burkitt lymphoma.

wrong_choice_explanations.2: BCR-ABL1 is characteristic of chronic myeloid leukemia and a subset of acute lymphoblastic leukemia.
wrong_choice_explanations.3: Isolated 5q deletion is associated with a myelodysplastic syndrome, not Burkitt lymphoma.
wrong_choice_explanations.4: t(14;18) with BCL2 overexpression is characteristic of follicular lymphoma and suppresses apoptosis rather than producing classic Burkitt biology.
wrong_choice_explanations.5: Cyclin D1 translocation is typical of mantle-cell lymphoma.

questions.educational_objective: Recognize Burkitt lymphoma from rapid growth, starry-sky histology, and very high Ki-67, and connect it to immunoglobulin-enhancer-driven MYC overexpression.
